incident.what: A vector store's DELETE marked rows as tombstones. The database file did not shrink; orphan vectors stayed; a full table rebuild was required. Separately: embeddings are lossy but invertible, so 'we only store vectors' is not a privacy boundary.
incident.signal: A collaborator's field report on a SQLite vector extension.

root_cause: 'Delete returned success' was taken to mean 'the data is gone'.

law.text: Acceptance of forgetting is measured, not reported: zero orphans, zero freelist growth, file size not increased. Vectors never leave the trust boundary and are encrypted at rest.
checks: post-delete: file size <= pre-delete size after vacuum
vector store is inside the same boundary as the raw text it encodes

notes: De-identified from a real operating incident. Names, systems and paths removed; the mechanism is kept.
